scope: Structural comparison is all 46 FX programs; basic rendering below is the 22 original-address programs only.

programs.name: Ring Bell
programs.description: A rounded wooden-mode body supports a short metallic upper mallet, then feeds the ring circuit. Hard strikes expose the upper clang; its rapid losses leave a softer resonating body behind. A gently open body, a defined attack and a clean key release.

programs.name: Laser Sweep
programs.description: A low body and later upper pulse bloom as the ring carrier rises, then falls over several seconds. Different filter and amplitude swells make the motion unfold in layers. A quick, forward edge that settles into a more compact body.

programs.name: Amber FX 137
programs.description: A steady 16' pulse motor supports a quieter upper mechanical buzz. A fixed 50 Hz ring carrier supplies sidebands, with a gradual start and a short coast after release. A warm main body with a slightly longer decay; the separate attack stays concise.

programs.name: Velvet FX 138
programs.description: An airy gust enters before the broad low wind bed. Independently paced smooth random filter and level motion forms uneven gusts, without a repeating SUB pulse; pressure raises the upper air, which subsides before the low bed. A covered upper register and rounded main release, preserving the shorter edge.

programs.name: Distant FX 139
programs.description: A very slow 16' sine bloom carries a later, cloudy noise band. Gentle sub-hertz ring beating and long independent releases leave a deep, moving tail. A subdued upper edge over a longer body ending; characteristic body detail remains present.

programs.name: Neon FX 140
programs.description: A high narrow pulse alternates pitches at 7 Hz, with a sharper 2' onset edge. Brief release and shallow level pulses keep the electronic signal dry and articulated. A forward attack color with a compact main decay and a separately controlled accent.

programs.name: Hollow FX 141
programs.description: A voiced ah-formant body carries a fixed 73 Hz mechanical ring, with a brief noisy saw consonant above it. The vocal resonances retain their shape across pitch changes; pressure opens and raises the sustained robotic vowel. A lightly focused filter band over a longer body, with restrained resonance on acoustic models.

programs.name: Golden FX 142
programs.description: Six-Hz retriggered envelopes make short mechanical ticks from a high pulse and thin noise edge. Each tick falls silent before the next; slower SUB filter steps alternate the tick-tock color, and held chords cycle through their keyed pitches. A gently open body, a defined attack and a clean key release.

programs.name: Frozen FX 143
programs.description: A continuous rain bed supports fine upper droplets. Fast raised-cosine random intensity contours combine with independent slower filter and level movement, keeping the rainfall fluid rather than switching the whole bed in clocked steps. Steadier tuning and a longer body decay, without stretching a separate short strike.

programs.name: Electric FX 144
programs.description: A resonant pulse sweep drops sharply after the strike, with no bypass sine masking the descent. A separate, very short noise flash adds the laser's initial snap. A quick, forward edge that settles into a more compact body.

programs.name: Midnight FX 145
programs.description: A dark 16' saw-and-sine foundation supports a later third-harmonic pulse. Slow ring beating and gentle filter drift animate the held drone without a sharp attack. A dark upper contour with a slightly lingering body; the onset remains defined.

programs.name: Slow FX 146
programs.description: A low body and later upper pulse bloom as the ring carrier rises, then falls over several seconds. Different filter and amplitude swells make the motion unfold in layers. A slower main entrance and longer ending, preserving the source's brief accents.

programs.name: Bright FX 147
programs.description: A resonant saw-and-noise body follows a short high noise scrape. The ring carrier falls quickly after impact, adding a rough metallic edge to the closing filter bands. A more open upper contour with a clear accent and slightly tighter main decay.

programs.name: Dark FX 148
programs.description: A brief broadband crack precedes a slower low rumble with a long falling tail. Smooth random intensity and spectral changes make the roll uneven without periodic pumping; broad low resonance avoids a fixed pitched boom, and velocity controls the impact. A covered upper contour with a tidy ending, retaining the instrument body's defining modes.

programs.name: Wide FX 149
programs.description: One breaking wave unfolds per note: the low surge rises first, brighter spray blooms later, and the foam drains away ahead of the long low wash. Independent one-shot envelopes shape the wave without a cyclic amplitude or filter pulse. Complementary ranks spread across stereo with a restrained, register-appropriate width and a centered composite image.

programs.name: Soft FX 150
programs.description: An 11 Hz sample-and-hold source picks resonant bubble colors while two independent smooth random level contours make the pops uneven in strength. A hollow pulse body and a little filtered noise keep their separate rounded and airy edges. A restrained upper contour and a cushioned main entrance; struck instruments retain their articulation.

programs.name: Amber FX 151
programs.description: A rounded wooden-mode body supports a short metallic upper mallet, then feeds the ring circuit. Hard strikes expose the upper clang; its rapid losses leave a softer resonating body behind. A warm main body with a slightly longer decay; the separate attack stays concise.

programs.name: Velvet FX 152
programs.description: A sine body and quiet octave harmonic follow a smooth three-semitone peak-to-peak SUB wail. Rounded onset and release avoid clicks; pressure quickens the siren. The pure sine has a cushioned entrance and a broader pressure-shaped ending.

programs.name: Distant FX 153
programs.description: A low sine body follows repeating downward SUB glides while the shared ring carrier settles over the phrase. Release all keys and any sustain hold before the next attack to restart that sweep; a shorter upper pulse edge marks each note. A subdued upper edge over a longer body ending; characteristic body detail remains present.

programs.name: Neon FX 154
programs.description: A clear 4' call alternates between two pitches three semitones apart. A quieter low pulse gives the onset weight while square SUB level motion accents the two-tone warning. A forward attack color with a compact main decay and a separately controlled accent.

programs.name: Hollow FX 155
programs.description: Modern sample-and-hold steps the resonant filters at 7.5 Hz. A saw body and lighter octave pulse make each held random cutoff audible as a computer-like burble. A lightly focused filter band over a longer body, with restrained resonance on acoustic models.

programs.name: Golden FX 156
programs.description: Hold a note for a long resonant rise: the low saw opens broadly before the later noise crest blooms above it. The slower filter entrance and restrained resonance keep the rising band defined without an abrupt early whistle; its peak settles gradually. A gently open body, a defined attack and a clean key release.

programs.name: Random Filter
programs.description: Modern sample-and-hold steps the resonant filters at 7.5 Hz. A saw body and lighter octave pulse make each held random cutoff audible as a computer-like burble.

programs.name: Random Pitch Blips
programs.description: Modern sample-and-hold picks small, unquantized pitch steps around the played key at 6.5 Hz. A matching square amplitude LFO separates the sine-and-pulse tone into blips.

programs.name: Siren

programs.description: A soft low breath band supports a faster upper-air layer. Pressure raises the airy rank more strongly and gently opens both filters, giving a controllable exhale and fade.
